text: Implement func Clamp(v, lo, hi int) int in internal/num/num.go returning v bounded to [lo,hi]. Single file, complete spec.
Write func WordWrap(s string, width int) []string breaking on spaces, never mid-word. One file.
Add func ParseSemver(s string) (major, minor, patch int, err error) following semver 2.0 core rules. One file.
Create internal/csv/writer.go with func Write(rows [][]string) string, quoting any field containing a comma or quote.
Implement func Encode(b []byte) string using the standard base64 alphabet with padding, in one new file.
Add func (l *List) Reverse() to internal/list/list.go, reversing nodes in place. Spec complete.
Write func Median(xs []float64) float64 returning the median; define it as the mean of the two middle values for even length.
Add a String() method to the Duration type formatting as '1h2m3s', omitting zero components.
Implement func Chunk[T any](xs []T, n int) [][]T splitting a slice into runs of at most n.
Rename the variable tmp to buf throughout internal/io/reader.go.
Add a package doc comment to internal/queue describing the ring-buffer semantics already implemented.
Write func IsPalindrome(s string) bool ignoring case and non-letter runes.
Implement func Dedup(xs []string) []string preserving first-occurrence order.
Add func RomanToInt(s string) int handling the standard subtractive pairs. One file, full spec.
Format internal/config/config.go with gofmt and fix the two lint warnings it reports.
Write a table-driven test for the existing func Clamp covering lo>hi, equal bounds, and in-range values.
Add func BytesHuman(n int64) string rendering 1536 as '1.5 KiB', binary units, one decimal.
Implement func Flatten(xs [][]int) []int concatenating in order. Single function.
Create func Title(s string) string upper-casing the first letter of each space-separated word.
Add func SumBy[T any](xs []T, f func(T) int) int returning the total. One file.
Write func Unique(xs []int) bool reporting whether all elements differ.
Implement func TrimComment(line string) string removing a trailing // comment not inside a string literal.
Replace every GORM query in the services/ tree with the new sqlc-generated accessors, keeping behaviour identical.
Refactor the auth middleware across the api/ package to use the new session store and update every call site.
Add a /v2/reports endpoint alongside the existing v1 one, reusing the existing handler where sensible.
Make the export feature work better for large accounts; work out what that should mean from the current code.
Integrate the billing service with the existing Stripe webhook handler; requirements aren't fully specified.
Migrate the logging calls in cmd/ from log to slog, preserving the existing field names.
Wire the new feature-flag client into the request path so handlers can read flags without extra plumbing.
Move the retry logic out of the HTTP client and into a shared package used by both the API and the worker.
Update the CLI so every subcommand accepts --json, matching whatever format the existing report command uses.
Add pagination to the reports endpoint, following whatever convention the other list endpoints already use.
Extract the duplicated validation in the three handlers into one helper and use it everywhere.
Make the importer tolerate the legacy CSV layout as well as the current one; infer the legacy shape from old fixtures.
Change the cache key scheme across the read path so tenant IDs are included, and update everything that reads it.
Port the settings page to the new form component, keeping the current validation behaviour.
Rework the worker so it processes batches instead of single items, keeping the existing at-least-once guarantee.
Add support for the new config file location while continuing to read the old one.
Thread a context through the storage layer so callers can cancel long reads.
Adapt the exporter to the upstream API's v3 response shape; the changes aren't documented, read the client code.
Split the god-object Service type into two, keeping the public API unchanged.
Make the tests run against both sqlite and postgres, reusing the current fixtures.
Update every call site after adding a required ctx parameter to the Store interface.
Convert the polling loop to the new event subscription, matching current delivery semantics.
Requests intermittently return stale data only under load; nobody can reproduce it locally. Find the cause.
Review our password reset token generation and fix anything that lets an attacker forge one.
Choose and justify a replication and failover strategy for the new metadata store.
Users report intermittent double-charging under concurrent retries in the payment reconciliation job. Find the root cause.
Audit the OAuth token refresh flow for privilege escalation and fix any vulnerability you find.
Design the sharding and consistency model for our multi-region write path.
A goroutine leak shows up only after ~6 hours in production. Track it down.
Decide whether to move the job queue from Postgres to Kafka, and justify the choice against our durability needs.
Our JWT validation accepts tokens it shouldn't in some edge case. Find and close the hole.
Design the migration path that lets us change the primary key type with zero downtime.
Occasional data corruption appears after a failover; determine whether the bug is in our code or the driver.
Harden the file upload path against path traversal and zip-slip, and prove the fix covers both.
Work out why p99 latency tripled after the last deploy when no query plan changed.
Design the tenancy isolation model so one tenant can never read another's rows, and justify it.
A deadlock appears under a specific interleaving of the scheduler and the cache. Diagnose it.
Evaluate whether our current encryption-at-rest scheme meets the requirement and change it if not.
Find why the reconciler occasionally writes a state the state machine says is unreachable.
Decide the consistency guarantees the new read-replica path should offer, and reshape the API around them.
Our rate limiter can be bypassed by a specific header combination. Find it and fix it.
Determine the cause of the memory growth that only appears with TLS session resumption enabled.
Design how we roll keys without invalidating in-flight sessions, and justify the tradeoffs.
Sessions occasionally get attributed to the wrong user under high concurrency. Find the root cause.
